questions.question_text: Identify the sentence that uses correct punctuation.
options: The students finished their work and went to recess.
The students finished their work, and went to recess.
The students finished their work and went to recess
The students finished their work and, went to recess.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, the conjunction 'and' connects two parts of a single predicate, so no comma is required.

questions.question_text: Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence: 'The team _____ practicing for the big game all week.'
questions.explanation: 'Team' is a collective noun acting as a single unit, so the singular verb 'has been' is correct.

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses the correct spelling?
questions.explanation: 'Experiment' is the standard correct spelling of the word.

questions.question_text: Which word completes the sentence: 'She _____ to the party later.'
questions.explanation: 'Will go' indicates a future action, which fits the context of 'later'.

questions.question_text: Which sentence has no spelling errors?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling follows the rule 'i before e, except after c'.

questions.question_text: Which phrase uses a correct homophone?
questions.explanation: 'They're' is the contraction of 'they are', which fits the sentence.
Days of the week, proper nouns, and the start of a sentence must always be capitalized.

options: Neither of the boys were present.
Neither of the boys was present.
Neither of the boys are present.
Neither of the boys been present.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' acts as a singular subject, requiring the singular verb 'was'.

questions.question_text: Which punctuation mark is missing in: 'The cars wheels were flat'
questions.explanation: An apostrophe is needed to show possession: 'car's'.

questions.question_text: Identify the adverb in the sentence: 'He spoke quietly to the crowd.'
questions.explanation: Adverbs modify verbs and often end in -ly. 'Quietly' describes how he spoke.

questions.question_text: Select the correct plural form of 'child'.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is the irregular plural form of the word 'child'.
